AWS outage in US-EAST-1 knocks Slack, Venmo and Ring offline

Published 2026-10-07 09:40 UTC

A widespread Amazon Web Services outage on Wednesday morning took down or degraded dozens of popular apps, including Slack, Venmo, Ring, Fortnite and Duolingo. The AWS Health Dashboard reported increased error rates and latencies for multiple services in the US-EAST-1 region in northern Virginia, the company's oldest and largest.

Engineers identified elevated error rates for DynamoDB as the starting point, which cascaded to EC2, Lambda and other services that depend on it. Downdetector logged more than four million problem reports worldwide during the outage.

AWS said at 9:30 a.m. Eastern that it was seeing early signs of recovery but that some services would take longer to fully recover as backlogs cleared. The outage is the largest since a similar US-EAST-1 incident in 2021 and renews questions about how much of the internet depends on a single cloud region.

Startups that rely entirely on Amazon's cloud described a frustrating morning. Founders posted on social media that their applications were down and that they could not reach Amazon support because the support portal was struggling too. Several said they were reconsidering their reliance on a single region after the incident.

The outage affected core services including compute instances, databases and serverless functions in US-EAST-1. Because many other Amazon services depend on those components internally, problems spread to features that customers may not realize were tied to the region, such as some global authentication and console functions.

Ring said its doorbells and cameras could not send notifications or stream video during the outage, though recording continued locally on some models. Slack said messages were delayed and file uploads failed. Venmo said payments were delayed but that no money was lost, and that transactions would complete once systems recovered.

Amazon has faced several major outages in the US-EAST-1 region over the years. After each one, the company published a detailed explanation and listed changes it made to prevent a repeat. Customers will be watching for a similar report this time, along with any service credits offered under the company's service level agreements.
